chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, all from Hanan ibn Sadir, from his father, who said:

I, my father, my grandfather, and my uncle entered a bathhouse in Medina, and there was a man in the dressing room. He said to us, 'From whom are the people?' We said, 'From the people of Iraq.' He said, 'And from which part of Iraq?' We said, 'We are Kufans.' He said, 'Welcome to you, O people of Kufa. You are wearing clothes and are without a towel.' Then he said, 'What prevents you from using the loincloth? For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The nakedness of the believer upon the believer is prohibited.'

He said, 'He sent a cloth to my father, so he tore it into four pieces. Then each one of us took one, and we entered into it. When we were in the hot room, he turned towards my grandfather and said, 'O elderly man, what prevents you from dyeing (your beard)?' My grandfather said to him, 'I was with someone who was better than me and you, and he did not dye.' He said, 'He became angry because of that, to the extent that we recognized his anger in the bathhouse.' He said, 'And who is that who is better than me?' He said, 'I was with Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and he did not dye.' He said, 'So he bowed his head and sweat poured out, and he said, 'You have spoken the truth and been righteous.'

Then he said, 'O elderly man, if you dye, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had dyed, and he was better than Ali (peace be upon him). And if you leave it, then for you is the Sunnah of Ali (peace be upon him).'
He said, 'When we exited the bathhouse, we asked about the man, and it was Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and with him was his son Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.عَوْرَةُ الْمُؤْمِنِ: The private parts/nakedness of the believer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dyeing the beard according to the practice of the Prophet and Imam Ali in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the scholarly tradition of *Adab al-Mir'ah* (manners in the bathhouse), where Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) engages Kufan travelers on modesty and the specific practice of dyeing the beard. It illustrates the nuanced Shia understanding of prophetic sunnah by contrasting the Prophet’s use of henna with Imam Ali’s preference for leaving the beard natural, demonstrating that both are valid expressions of piety. The narrative underscores the transmission of religious etiquette through direct, personal interaction within the Ahl al-Bayt.
